title: Set 204

sentences.ko: 이번 주말에 집 밖으로 한 번도 안 나갔어. 좀 죄책감이 들 줄 알았는데 안 들더라. 아무도 나한테 뭘 바라지 않는 이틀이 그냥 정말 필요했나 봐.
sentences.text: I didn't leave the apartment once this weekend, and I kind of thought I'd feel guilty about it, but I don't. I think I just really needed two days where nobody needed anything from me.

alts.text: Didn't step outside all weekend. Figured I'd feel bad about it, but nope. Guess I just needed two days where nobody wanted anything from me.
I did not leave the apartment at all this weekend, and I expected to feel guilty about it, but I do not. I believe I simply needed two days in which no one required anything of me.

sentences.note: **kind of** 는 말을 살짝 흐릴 때 붙이는 말로, 좀, 약간 정도의 뜻입니다. **feel guilty about** 는 ~에 대해 죄책감이 들다라는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 주말에 아무것도 안 하고 쉰 게 좋았다고 말하기

sentences.ko: 그래서 결국 허리 때문에 병원에 갔거든. 엑스레이 찍으라고 하거나 뭐 그럴 줄 알았는데, 의사가 그냥 책상 의자가 너무 낮다고, 좀 더 자주 일어나서 걸어 다니라고 하더라. 아내가 1년 내내 하던 말을 40달러 내고 들은 거지.
sentences.text: So I finally went to the doctor about my back, and I was sure they'd send me for X-rays or something, but she just said my desk chair's too low and I need to get up and walk around more. So I paid forty bucks to hear what my wife's been telling me for a year.

alts.text: Finally got my back checked out. Thought for sure they'd want X-rays, but nope, she says my desk chair's too low and I gotta get up and move more. Forty bucks to hear what my wife's been saying for a year!

I finally consulted the doctor about my back, and I was certain I would be sent for X-rays, but she simply said that my desk chair is too low and that I need to stand up and walk around more often. I paid forty dollars to hear what my wife has been telling me for a year.

sentences.note: **I was sure** 는 분명히 ~일 줄 알았다는 뜻으로, 예상이 빗나갔을 때 자주 씁니다. **forty bucks** 의 buck 은 달러를 편하게 부르는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 병원 갔다 온 얘기 가볍게 하기

sentences.ko: 그 비싼 믹서기는 정말 사지 말걸 그랬어. 출근 전에 스무디 만들어 먹으려고 샀는데, 너무 시끄러워서 온 식구가 다 깨. 그래서 지금은 그냥 조리대 위에 놓여만 있어.
sentences.text: I really wish I hadn't bought that fancy blender. I got it so I could make smoothies before work, but it's so loud it wakes up the whole house, so now it's just sitting there on the counter.

alts.text: Man, I shouldn't have bought that fancy blender. Got it for smoothies before work, but it's so loud it wakes everybody up, so now it just sits on the counter.

I sincerely regret purchasing that expensive blender. I bought it so that I could make smoothies before work, but it is so loud that it wakes the entire household, so it now sits unused on the counter.

sentences.note: **I wish I hadn't bought** 는 사지 말걸 그랬다는 후회를 나타냅니다. **just sitting there** 는 쓰지 않고 그냥 놓여만 있다는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 변기 고치는 법 좀 알아보려고 유튜브에 들어간 건데, 어쩌다 보니 두 시간 뒤에 웬 아저씨가 낡은 배 고치는 영상을 보고 있더라. 아 그리고 변기는 아직도 물이 계속 안 멈춰.
sentences.text: I only went on YouTube to figure out how to fix the toilet, and somehow two hours later I was watching some guy restore an old boat. And the toilet's still running, by the way.

alts.text: All I wanted was a video on fixing the toilet, and two hours later I'm watching some dude restore an old boat. Toilet's still running, by the way.
I only went on YouTube to learn how to repair the toilet, and somehow, two hours later, I was watching a man restore an old boat. The toilet is, incidentally, still running.

sentences.note: **somehow** 는 어쩌다 보니, 나도 모르게라는 뜻입니다. 변기가 **still running** 이라는 말은 물이 멈추지 않고 계속 흐른다는 뜻이고, **by the way** 는 아 그리고, 참고로처럼 말을 덧붙일 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: 유튜브 보다가 시간 다 날린 얘기

sentences.ko: 이사할지 말지 계속 왔다 갔다 하고 있어. 3월에 월세가 200달러 오르니까 나가는 게 맞긴 한데, 또 짐 다 싸고 애들 새 학교 알아볼 생각을 하면 그냥 여기 눌러살고 싶어.
sentences.text: We keep going back and forth about moving. The rent's going up two hundred dollars in March, so it'd make sense to leave, but then I think about packing everything up again and finding the kids a new school, and I just want to stay put.

alts.text: We can't make up our minds about moving. Rent's going up two hundred bucks in March, so leaving makes sense, but then I picture packing it all up again and finding the kids a new school, and I'm like, nah, let's just stay.

We continue to go back and forth about whether to move. Our rent will increase by two hundred dollars in March, so leaving would be sensible, but when I consider packing everything once more and finding a new school for the children, I would simply prefer to remain where we are.

sentences.note: **go back and forth** 는 마음을 못 정하고 이랬다저랬다 한다는 뜻입니다. **stay put** 은 옮기지 않고 그 자리에 그대로 있다는 뜻입니다.

reviewed: 4번 한국어: running toilet 은 물이 새는 것이 아니라 물이 멈추지 않고 계속 흐르는 것이라 '물이 계속 새' 를 '물이 계속 안 멈춰' 로 고침
